title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: production workloads showed fairness regressions and unbounded queue wait times under mixed-priority traffic. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation of low-priority small requests, and add configurable request timeouts/aging. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce multi-tier priority queues with configurable weights and an aging factor so low-priority requests steadily increase effective priority the longer they wait; 2) Add a max_wait_time policy and per-request deadline propagation so stale requests are dropped early and do not block capacity; 3) Dynamic slot allocation between interactive and throughput pools based on short-window latency SLOs; 4) KV cache eviction hint integration so long-waiting requests with KV hits are prioritized to reduce wasted work; 5) New metrics and tracing spans for queue depth, age histogram, priority-rebalance events, and per-priority p95/p99; 6) Extensive unit and load tests plus an end-to-end performance benchmark harness. Backwards compatible: defaults preserve prior behavior; new knobs are exposed via continuous_batcher config (weighting, aging_factor_ms, max_wait_ms, interactive_slots_pct). See related Linear tasks ENG-321/ENG-322 and support ticket SUP-1101 for incident context.
commits_summary: refactor(scheduler): extract priority-queue abstraction and basic interfaces
feat(continuous-batcher): add aging factor and max_wait_time enforcement
perf(scheduler): dynamic slot allocator for interactive/throughput pools
feat(kv-cache): add eviction_hint to request metadata and prioritization path
test(scheduler): unit tests for aging and fairness under synthetic load
ci(tests): add perf canary job targeting mixed-priority traces
docs: update continuous-batcher config reference and changelog
review_comments: Miguel Torres (reviewer): The aging approach looks promising, but can we bound the effective priority to avoid priority inversion from very old requests?

Ava Chen (author): Added a cap (max_effective_priority) in priority_weighting.go and wired it to config; default preserves previous ordering. See commit 'feat: cap effective priority (weighting cap)'.
Priya Patel (reviewer): There are several hot loops in the allocator that might be contended at high concurrency. Can you add contention metrics or microbenchmarks?
Ava Chen (author): Added allocator contention metrics and a microbenchmark to scheduler_test.go. Observed <2% throughput impact; included numbers in perf_summary below.

Ethan Zhao (reviewer): How does this interact with the KV cache rehydration path when a request is prioritized but misses the cache? We need to avoid thrashing cache population for low-value requests.

Ava Chen (author): Implemented eviction_hint and conservative policy: only prioritize KV-hit hints or requests above size threshold when cache rehits are likely. Documented tradeoffs in README and added tests.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge. Squash commit message: 'continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts — refs ENG-321, ENG-322'
perf_summary: p95 latency (mixed workload) reduced from 210ms to 165ms (-21%) across 50k rps canary
p99 tail latency reduced from 480ms to 360ms (-25%)
overall throughput unchanged (+0.5%), but observed 35% reduction in unfair queuing incidents (requests waiting > max_wait_ms)
CPU overhead for allocator and priority weighting ~+1.7% in canary microbenchmarks; tradeoff accepted for latency/fairness gains
release_notes: Scheduler: continuous-batcher gains configurable multi-tier priority queues, aging to prevent starvation, max_wait_time enforcement, dynamic slot allocation, and KV cache prioritization hints. Default behavior unchanged. Config knobs: aging_factor_ms, max_wait_ms, interactive_slots_pct, priority_weights.
notes_for_ops: Rollback: flip feature flags in continuous_batcher config or revert chart value 'continuousBatcher.scheduler.enabled'. If experiencing regressions, reduce aging_factor_ms to 0 to restore strict priority behavior. Observe new metrics: cb_queue_age_histogram, cb_priority_rebalance_count.
